problem: Find the radius of the curvature for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at $t=0.$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

The radius of curvature $R$ is defined as
$R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}.$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)={e}^{t},\,y(t)={e}^{-t}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =-{e}^{-t} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{″}(t) & ={e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-(-{e}^{-t})\cdot {e}^{t}|}{{(({e}^{t})^{2}+(-{e}^{-t})^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{({e}^{2t}+{e}^{-2t})}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =\frac{2}{{({e}^{2(0)}+{e}^{-2(0)})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{2}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{1}{κ(0)}=\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
